chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who forgot to wipe over his head, then remembered while he was in the salat (prayer), he said:

“If he is certain of that, he should break off, wipe over his head and over his feet, and then begin the salat (prayer) anew. But if he doubts and does not know whether he wiped or did not wipe, then let him take from his beard, if it is moist, and wipe over his head; and if there is water before him, then let him take from it and wipe his head with it.”

key_terms.اسْتَيْقَنَ: became certain, meaning he has definite knowledge of the omission
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) during which the omission was remembered
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, the place requiring wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his feet, which are also to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.شَكَّ: doubted, meaning he was uncertain whether the wiping had occurred
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: his beard, from whose moisture wiping may be performed
key_terms.مُبْتَلَّةً: moist or wet, indicating usable moisture for wiping
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe, referring here to the masḥ required in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he remembers during salat (prayer) that he forgot to wipe his head in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who remembers during salat (prayer) that he may have omitted wiping the head in wudu (ablution). If he is certain he omitted it, he must leave the prayer, complete the wiping of the head and feet, and then restart the salat (prayer); if he is unsure, he may wipe his head using remaining moisture from his beard or available water.
